content.value_statement: DeFi registry changes often require synchronized edits across several frontend, backend, shared, and Rust files. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code checklists and templates for complete token, protocol, chain, and RPC updates.
actual_capabilities: Identifies which registry files must change for tokens, protocols, chains, and networks.
Provides token templates for frontend constants, Rust core data, wallet services, and symbol maps.
Guides RPC and WebSocket endpoint configuration for supported blockchain networks.
Lists validation commands for checking token counts, address consistency, and address typos.
Highlights critical DeFi data rules such as decimals, checksum addresses, and fallback RPCs.
limitations: Does not verify live token metadata or contract addresses without separate tooling.
Does not add registry entries automatically unless the agent edits the target project files.
Assumes the target codebase uses the file layout described in the skill.
Does not manage secrets or provision RPC provider accounts.

use_cases.title: Add a token consistently
use_cases.description: Use the token checklist to update frontend, Rust, wallet, symbol, and decimal registries together.

use_cases.title: Introduce a new chain
use_cases.description: Follow the chain checklist to add chain IDs, network constants, RPC settings, token entries, and protocol addresses.

use_cases.title: Review registry completeness
use_cases.description: Compare planned registry changes against the required files and validation steps before shipping.

prompt_templates.title: Add a basic token
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DeFi registry manager to add TOKEN on Ethereum. Show every file that must change and ask me for any missing address or decimals data.

prompt_templates.title: Add a new protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DeFi registry manager to add a new DEX named PROTOCOL. Identify frontend, shared, arbitrage, and oracle updates before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a new chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DeFi registry manager to add support for CHAIN_NAME. Include chain ID, RPC variables, block timing, gas settings, and token registry follow-up work.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a registry change set
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DeFi registry manager to review my pending registry changes. Check consistency across token lists, decimals, protocol addresses, RPC settings, and validation commands.

output_examples.input: Add USDC on a new supported chain.
output: Checklist of required files across frontend, Rust core, wallet service, and shared schema.
Questions for contract address, decimals, checksum format, and chain support.
Validation steps for address consistency and token count checks.

output_examples.input: Add an RPC endpoint for Arbitrum.
output: Environment variable names for HTTP and WebSocket endpoints.
Server and database fields that should store RPC and explorer configuration.
Connectivity and rate-limit checks to run before deployment.

output_examples.input: Review whether a DEX registry update is complete.
output: Missing registry locations grouped by frontend, server, shared schema, and oracle support.
Validation commands to confirm references and catch address typos.

best_practices: Verify token addresses and decimals from authoritative sources before editing registry files.
Update every listed registry location in the same change set to avoid runtime mismatches.
Run build and validation checks for both TypeScript and Rust components after changes.
anti_patterns: Do not add a token to only the frontend list and skip server or Rust registries.
Do not guess token decimals, because incorrect decimals can break balances and trades.
Do not commit real RPC keys or provider secrets into source files.

faq.question: What does this skill help manage?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate registry updates for DeFi tokens, protocols, DEXes, chains, networks, RPC endpoints, and validation steps.

faq.question: Can it verify token addresses automatically?
faq.answer: No. It reminds the agent to verify addresses, but verification needs trusted explorers or project-specific tooling.

faq.question: Does it support both TypeScript and Rust files?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill lists TypeScript, shared schema, server, frontend, and Rust registry locations.

faq.question: Is it only for adding new tokens?
faq.answer: No. It also covers new protocols, DEXes, chains, networks, RPC settings, and address updates.

faq.question: Does it store RPC credentials?
faq.answer: No. It documents environment variable patterns and warns that real provider keys should not be committed.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
